務.meaning: A sailor gets her list of chores: polish the <part>harpoon</part>, wave a big <part>fan</part> at the sails when the wind dies, and haul the ropes with every <part>muscle</part> she has. Tick, tick, tick. Each line on the list is a <kanji>task</kanji>.
務.on: Last job of the day: shoo a <sound>moo</sound>se off the deck.
務.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes in the spray, then scrubs the <sound>to</sound>tem pole carved on the bow: she works hard.

制.meaning: On a very strict dairy farm, every <part>cow</part> is milked at six, rubbed down with its own numbered <part>towel</part> at seven, and has its hooves trimmed with a tiny <part>dagger</part> at eight. Nothing ever happens out of order. It all runs on one big <kanji>system</kanji>.
制.on: Each night, the farmer locks the towels in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.

要.meaning: A <part>woman</part> rides a camel <part>west</part> across the desert with one tiny bag. No books, no spare shoes, no snacks: only water and a map, the two things she must have. That's all she'll <kanji>need</kanji>.
要.on: Well, one more thing: a <sound>yo</sound>-yo for the long nights.
要.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' she squeals when the camel drinks all her water. Now she needs more.

記.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> sways at the foot of the king's throne. As the king makes his <part>speech</part>, it scratches every word into the sand with the tip of its tail, never missing one. It's the royal <kanji>scribe</kanji>.
記.on: When the speech ends, it locks the words in a chest and swallows the <sound>key</sound>.
記.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p reads it all aloud, while a <sound>roo</sound>k copies it onto paper: written down.

籍.meaning: At the oldest farm school, each new student carves her name on a strip of <part>bamboo</part>, ties it to a rusty <part>plough</part> from <part>antiquity</part>, and drags it once round the field. Now her name is on the list for good. That's how you <kanji>enroll</kanji>.
籍.on: The field is split like a pie chart, one <sound>sec</sound>tor ploughed for each new class.

義.meaning: A wolf with a huge <part>ego</part> struts into the meadow and eats the flock's grass. One small <part>sheep</part> stands up, marches him to the village court and makes him plant it all back, blade by blade. Right beats might: that's <kanji>justice</kanji>.
義.on: The court clock ticks on, every <sound>gea</sound>r turning, as the wolf digs.

反.meaning: A grumpy <part>pretzel</part> lives under a <part>cliff</part> and disagrees with everything. Say up, it says down. Say twist, it untwists. It even waves a tiny banner that just says NO. It's <kanji>anti</kanji> everything.
反.on: Offer it <sound>hon</sound>ey and it demands mustard instead.
反.kun: It even bends over backwards on the arm of a <sound>so</sound>fa, just to be different: warped.

備.meaning: Before climbing the <part>cliff</part>, a hiker takes rope and boots off a <part>coat hook</part>, packs a tuft of <part>grass</part> for her goat, and leans a <part>fence</part> panel on the rock as a ladder. Rope, boots, snack, ladder: she knows how to <kanji>equip</kanji> a climb.
備.on: A <sound>bee</sound>tle rides along in her pocket as a lucky charm.
備.kun: The night before, she lays it all out on the <sound>so</sound>fa, with a packed lunch of <sound>na</sound>an.

準.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> fills its birdbath with <part>water drops</part>, one beakful at a time, and checks the mark painted on the side: <part>ten</part> means full. It stops at five, hops in and splashes about anyway. Half full is still a bath: a <kanji>semi</kanji>-bath.
準.on: Afterwards it dries its wings in a prickly <sound>jun</sound>iper bush.
準.kun: Its chicks copy every move in the <sound>jun</sound>iper, splash for splash.

次.meaning: A bored penguin queues on the <part>ice</part> and lets out a huge <part>yawn</part>. At last the ticket man points his way: you're up. 'Who's <kanji>next</kanji>?' he calls, and the penguin waddles forward.
次.on: It climbs into a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p for a ride across the ice.
次.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the next in line, a goose with a gaggle of <sound>gee</sound>se behind it.

政.meaning: Two mayors argue in the town square, each flapping a giant <part>fan</part> and shouting that they alone are <part>correct</part>. The crowd takes sides, the fans flap harder, and nothing gets done. Welcome to <kanji>politics</kanji>.
政.on: Whoever wins gets the key to the town <sound>sa</sound>fe.
政.kun: A lla<sound>ma</sound> joins the race, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and promises a coral <sound>ree</sound>f to every <sound>go</sound>pher in town and a <sound>to</sound>tem pole for every park.

曇.meaning: The <part>sun</part> is sunbathing, when a fat grey <part>cloud</part> plops down on top of it like a cat on a warm laptop. Shadows spread, the picnic blankets are packed up, and the light goes dull. The sky starts to <kanji>cloud up</kanji>.
曇.on: A <sound>don</sound>key at the picnic grumbles, then eats all the sandwiches left behind.
曇.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k shoos a <sound>mo</sound>le off the cake as the sky turns grey.

露.meaning: A snail wakes to find the garden <part>path</part> sparkling, though no <part>rain</part> fell overnight. Every blade of grass along it wears tiny glass beads. The snail slurps one up for breakfast: fresh <kanji>dew</kanji>.
露.on: A <sound>ro</sound>dent scurries along behind it, leaving tiny wet footprints.
露.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' the snail sneezes, splashing a drop onto a <sound>yu</sound>zu lying in the grass.

濯.meaning: A <part>peacock</part> opens a launderette. Customers drop off their socks, and it swishes them through <part>water drops</part> with its huge tail, then fans them dry. Clean and folded in an hour: the best <kanji>laundry</kanji> in town.
濯.on: It gets paid in food: one crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co per bag.
濯.kun: A <sound>su</sound>shi chef brings his apron, and another <sound>su</sound>shi chef brings his: the peacock rinses both.

犬.meaning: A <part>large</part> man spreads his arms wide for a hug, and a muddy <part>dot</part> lands on his shoulder: a paw print. Something has jumped up to lick his ear and is wagging all over him. It's a <kanji>dog</kanji>.
犬.on: It drags him back to its <sound>ken</sound>nel to share its blanket.
犬.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' he squeals, as it pushes him into a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k at the back.

献.meaning: Every summer a <part>dog</part> trots up from the <part>south</part> with a basket of warm figs in its mouth and lays it at the door of an old hermit's cave. It never asks for anything back. It's an <kanji>offering</kanji>.
献.on: The hermit builds it a <sound>ken</sound>nel out of the empty fig baskets.
献.kun: Next year it brings a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>te</sound>nt and a lla<sound>ma</sound>, and lays them down with a sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

状.meaning: A <part>dog</part> sits at the foot of a <part>climbing pole</part>, where it has sat for three years, refusing to move. Nobody changes anything: same dog, same pole, same spot every day. That's the <kanji>status quo</kanji>.
状.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey peeks out of its mother's pouch, sees the dog and decides not to bother either.

症.meaning: In a <part>leaky shed</part> clinic, a doctor runs down her list and every guess is <part>correct</part>: runny nose, sneezing, hot forehead. A drip from the roof lands on the patient's head. Yes, it's a cold: you've got all the <kanji>symptoms</kanji>.
症.on: To cheer him up, she puts on a puppet <sound>show</sound> with two tissues.

単.meaning: A knight's <part>armor</part> has a hundred buckles, and getting dressed takes all morning. One day a spark from the <part>fireworks</part> lands on it, and he throws the whole lot off. Now he wears one plain shirt with a hole for his head. Much more <kanji>simple</kanji>.
単.on: He strolls home through the dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, light as a feather.
単.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' he giggles, swinging round a <sound>to</sound>tem pole in his thin shirt. '<sound>Eh</sound>? Cold!' Just a single layer.

簡.meaning: A monk builds his home from four <part>bamboo</part> poles and leaves a wide <part>interval</part> between two of them for a door. No furniture, no clutter, just sunlight falling through the gap. He loves its <kanji>simplicity</kanji>.
簡.on: The only decoration is one pink <sound>car</sound>nation in a cup.
簡.kun: An <sound>e</sound>lephant offers him a sofa, but he shakes his head, picks a single stick to sit on and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': he chooses.

川.meaning: Three long lines run down the hillside side by side, like ribbons dropped from a giant's pocket. A paper boat is set down at the top and swirls along them all the way to the sea. You're looking at a <kanji>river</kanji>.
川.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try on the bridge salutes every paper boat that floats by.
川.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps at the boat, and the mouse sailing it yells '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

流.meaning: A lazy <part>squid</part> lets go of its rock and stretches out its trailing arms. The rushing <part>water drops</part> carry it along, past fish and boats, without one flick of its fins. It just rides the <kanji>current</kanji>.
流.on: At the river mouth it bumps into all its cousins: a squid <sound>reu</sound>nion!
流.kun: A <sound>na</sound>an stuffed with <sound>gar</sound>lic drifts past, and they all float after it.

鍵.meaning: A dragon sleeps on a mountain of <part>gold</part>, but it worries about thieves. So it melts one coin and sets out to <part>build</part> a tiny thing with teeth along one edge. Now only that fits the cave door: it's the <kanji>key</kanji>.
鍵.on: The dragon hides it in its pet's <sound>ken</sound>nel, where no thief would look.
鍵.kun: But a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the moat and a flock of <sound>gee</sound>se saw everything.

復.meaning: A broken <part>deck chair</part> rides the <part>chairlift</part> up to the carpenter at the top of the mountain. She glues its legs, paints it bright yellow and sends it back down as good as new. She can <kanji>restore</kanji> anything.
復.on: At the bottom it's hung back on its <sound>hoo</sound>k by the pool.
復.kun: A lla<sound>ma</sound> sits on it and snaps it, then offers a <sound>ta</sound>co to say sorry. Up the lift it goes again.

往.meaning: A <part>lord</part> refuses to walk anywhere, so a <part>chairlift</part> is strung from his castle over the hills. He rides it for days with a picnic on his lap, waving to the sheep below. It's his grand <kanji>journey</kanji>.
往.on: He stops for the night in the branches of a giant <sound>oa</sound>k.
往.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' he squeals at every bump, but on he goes.

波.meaning: A bear spreads an old fur <part>pelt</part> on the sea like a rug and lies down on it. The <part>water drops</part> lift and roll it, up and down, until the bear is bobbing far from shore. It's riding the <kanji>waves</kanji>.
波.on: It washes up next to a little beach <sound>hu</sound>t.
波.kun: It shares a warm <sound>na</sound>an with the <sound>mee</sound>rkat who runs the hut.

津.meaning: After a storm, a battered little boat spots a painter on the shore. With one huge <part>brush</part> she sweeps a calm curve into the <part>water drops</part>, and the waves inside it go flat. The boat glides in and rests at last. It has found a <kanji>haven</kanji>.
津.on: The sailor jumps ashore and bangs his <sound>shin</sound> on the dock.
津.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes, dripping wet, and the painter wraps him in a towel.

処.meaning: An office clerk finds a pile of junk in the hall: a broken <part>folding chair</part> and a wobbly <part>table</part>. She folds the chair flat, flips the table, and carries both out to the skip in one trip. Problem handled: she knows how to <kanji>dispose</kanji> of things.
処.on: Then she sells the screws to a junk <sound>sho</sound>p round the corner.
処.kun: Now there's room for a <sound>ko</sound>ala to carve a <sound>to</sound>tem pole while a <sound>ro</sound>dent watches: a nice place.

箋.meaning: A knight snaps his <part>spear</part> into a dozen neat pens and opens a little shop. On the shelves: thin <part>bamboo</part> paper, envelopes, labels and wax seals, stacked in tidy piles. He sells <kanji>stationery</kanji>.
箋.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try off duty buys a sheet to write home.
箋.kun: The knight sticks a label on a rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton and sings 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'

混.meaning: At a family party, all the <part>descendants</part>, from grandkids to great-great-grandkids, pour their own <part>water drops</part> into one big punch bowl: lemonade, tea, milk, juice. Grandma stirs it all together. It's quite a <kanji>mix</kanji>.
混.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down and gives it one more stir with its wing.
混.kun: Then a lla<sound>ma</sound> dips its head in and mixes in some hay.
